messages.content:
Assign the three-character ICD-10-AM principal diagnosis category. Here are worked examples, then the case to code.

Example 1
Hospital course: A 72-year-old man with a 50 pack-year smoking history was admitted with three days of worsening breathlessness and purulent sputum. Spirometry showed an FEV1/FVC ratio of 0.52. He was treated with nebulised bronchodilators, oral prednisolone and antibiotics for an infective exacerbation of his long-standing airflow limitation.
Answer: J44

Example 2
Hospital course: A 58-year-old man presented with crushing central chest pain radiating to the jaw. The electrocardiogram showed ST elevation in the anterior leads and high-sensitivity troponin rose from 40 to 2100 ng/L. He underwent primary percutaneous coronary intervention with a stent to the proximal left anterior descending artery.
Answer: I21

Example 3
Hospital course: A 34-year-old woman presented with fever, rigors, dysuria and right flank tenderness. Urine microscopy showed pyuria and culture grew Escherichia coli. Computed tomography showed a swollen right kidney with no abscess. She improved on intravenous ceftriaxone.
Answer: N10

Discharge Summary:

Patient Name: [redacted]

Age: 82

Reason for Hospitalization:
The patient presented to the emergency department with epigastric pain, heartburn, and nausea due to a large hiatus hernia with a portion of the stomach within the intrathoracic cavity.

Hospital Course:
The patient was admitted to the Observation department and was treated with nasogastric decompression, zero diet, fluid therapy, a prokinetic and a proton pump inhibitor, which resulted in clinical improvement. The patient was then discharged and advised to perform an upper endoscopy, but declined due to her age and multiple comorbidities.
Diagnosis: [diagnosis section withheld]
Treatment:
The patient received nasogastric decompression, zero diet, fluid therapy, a prokinetic and a proton pump inhibitor, which resulted in clinical improvement. The patient was advised to perform an upper endoscopy, but declined surgical intervention or any other invasive intervention.

Follow-up:
The patient was advised to continue with dietary advice and pharmacological treatment directed at her symptoms. A solid link with the family doctor was made, leading to the optimal possible resolution of the patient's symptoms and improved physical and mental well-being.

Disposition:
The patient was discharged with outpatient follow-up.
